member.name: T:Pinhole.Turn.TurnRejectException
member.summary: The server answered and refused: a definitive error response (437 allocation mismatch, 401 after re-auth, …) proving the credentials or allocation this client holds are unusable on that server. Distinct from a timeout or transport fault, which proves nothing — callers must treat this type as retire-the-client evidence and everything else as transient.

member.name: T:Pinhole.Turn.TurnClient
member.summary: A relayed connection through any RFC 5766 TURN server: allocate, refresh, permission and send/data indications over one UDP socket, authenticated with long-term credentials. No native dependencies. Allocation and permission refreshes run on a background loop; a 438 stale nonce is adopted and the request retried once. Inbound payloads surface via ; the address peers send to is .

member.name: P:Pinhole.Turn.TurnClient.LocalEndPoint
member.summary: Local endpoint of the relay socket, bound before the allocation handshake and valid as soon as the client exists. This is not the address peers should send to — that is .

member.name: P:Pinhole.Turn.TurnClient.Server
member.summary: The TURN server being relayed through, as passed to . The socket is connected to it; every packet this client exchanges goes to this endpoint only.

member.name: P:Pinhole.Turn.TurnClient.Username
member.summary: The long-term-credential username (RFC 5389) supplied at allocation.

member.name: P:Pinhole.Turn.TurnClient.Credential
member.summary: The long-term-credential secret supplied at allocation. Kept in plain memory for the client's whole life — it re-derives the integrity key whenever the server rotates its realm — so it cannot be scrubbed on dispose.

member.name: P:Pinhole.Turn.TurnClient.RelayedAddress
member.summary: The relayed address the server allocated: the address peers send to. Null until succeeds; fixed for the client's lifetime after that.

member.name: P:Pinhole.Turn.TurnClient.IsAlive
member.summary: False once the socket is gone: after , after a failed allocation, or after three consecutive failed allocation refreshes — the refresh loop closes the socket then so traffic fails visibly instead of black-holing. An internal flag, not a probe: a path that died quietly still reports true.

member.name: E:Pinhole.Turn.TurnClient.Received
member.summary: Raised with the origin peer and payload of every Data Indication. Handlers run synchronously on the dedicated receive thread — the same thread that completes permission and refresh transactions — so a slow handler stalls both directions of the client, and a throwing handler becomes an unhandled thread exception. Each payload array is a private copy and may be retained.

member.name: M:Pinhole.Turn.TurnClient.AllocateAsync(System.Net.IPEndPoint,System.String,System.String,System.Threading.CancellationToken)
member.summary: Allocates a relay on using long-term credentials: an unauthenticated Allocate first learns the realm and nonce, the authenticated retry allocates. On success starts the background refresh loop and returns a client with set. Each transaction waits at most 8 s; server error responses surface as . On any failure the socket is already closed — there is nothing left to dispose.

member.name: M:Pinhole.Turn.TurnClient.CreatePermissionAsync(System.Net.IPAddress,System.Threading.CancellationToken)
member.summary: Asks the server to accept traffic to and from . TURN permissions are per-IP, not per-port. A 438 stale nonce is adopted and the request rebuilt once with the fresh realm and nonce. Also records the peer so skips its own permission request while the entry is under 240 s old. Throws on error response or timeout.

member.name: M:Pinhole.Turn.TurnClient.SendAsync(System.ReadOnlyMemory{System.Byte},System.Net.IPEndPoint,System.Threading.CancellationToken)
member.summary: Sends to as a Send Indication, first creating or refreshing the peer's permission when it is unseen or its entry is 240 s old. The await — and any throw — covers only that permission request; the indication itself is unacknowledged fire-and-forget with no delivery guarantee, and a socket error on it is swallowed.

member.name: M:Pinhole.Turn.TurnClient.Send(System.ReadOnlySpan{System.Byte},System.Net.IPEndPoint)
member.summary: Raw fire-and-forget Send Indication: no permission handling, so the server silently drops the data unless the peer was already permitted via or . Never waits on the network — a UDP send is a buffer handoff — and a socket error is swallowed, not reported.

member.name: M:Pinhole.Turn.TurnClient.DisposeAsync
member.summary: Cancels the refresh loop and closes the socket; the receive thread notices within its 200 ms receive poll. No deallocation Refresh is sent, so the server holds the allocation open until its lifetime — 600 s unless the server negotiated otherwise — expires. Completes synchronously and is safe to call more than once.
